hook: Their boat was on fire and the engine would not stop.
narration: Their fishing boat was on fire, and the engine would not shut off.
Seven people were aboard, about eight miles off Oahu.
They radioed that the smoke was unbearable.
So they threw the raft in and abandoned ship.
A Coast Guard Hercules guided a boat crew to them.
From up high, a crew can spot a raft that boats at wave level miss.
A cutter stayed with the burning boat.
outcome: All seven were pulled from the raft and taken to shore.
title: Fishing boat on fire off Oahu, 7 aboard
description:
A Coast Guard HC-130 aircrew guided a Station Honolulu boat crew to seven people in a life raft after the fishing vessel Miss Emma caught fire about 8 miles off Ko'Olina, Oahu, on Sept. 17, 2019.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 1st Class Garth Booye and Petty Officer 2nd Class Ryan Perez, Air Station Barbers Point, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/709901/coast-guard-rescues-7-fire-aboard-miss-emma-off-oahu

facts.claim: HC-130 vectored the RB-M, all seven pulled from raft and ferried to shore
facts.source_quote: the HC-130 Hercules aircrew was able to vector in a 45-foot Response Boat-Medium (RB-M) from Small Boat Station Honolulu, and the boat crew successfully pulled all seven survivors from a liferaft and ferried them to shore

facts.claim: Cutter Joseph Gerczak stayed on scene so the burning vessel was not a hazard
facts.source_quote: remained on scene to ensure that the burning vessel did not become a hazard to local maritime traffic
